title: Create and view productions (US-1, part 1)
detail: Production creation, creator becomes director, My Productions and membership-restricted details. PR #5; issue #7.
issueBody:
As a director, I want to create a production and invite my company with roles, so that everyone works from one place.

Acceptance criteria:

- A logged-in user who submits a title at `/productions/new/` becomes the director of that production.
- A member sees that production on `/productions/`. Someone who is not a member gets 404.
- A director can invite an existing account by email and assign one role: director, stage manager, actor, or crew. That person then sees the production with that role.
- An actor who opens the invite form gets 404.

Creating a production and hiding it from non-members shipped in https://github.com/tkg9/656Final-daunting-horizon/pull/5. Invites are still open.

title: Paste script and split into scenes (US-2)
detail: Persist numbered scenes with headings and text; ACT/SCENE splitting and replacement tested. PR #5; issue #8. Line-level persistence is not yet built.
issueBody:
As a director, I want to paste in the script and have it split into scenes, so that rehearsals and cues can refer to scenes.

Acceptance criteria:

- A director or stage manager can paste a script on the production's script page.
- The script splits into scenes on lines that begin with ACT or SCENE. Text before the first heading becomes scene 1.
- Replacing the script replaces the scenes.
- An actor who posts a script gets 404.

Shipped in https://github.com/tkg9/656Final-daunting-horizon/pull/5.

title: AI character breakdown (US-3, part 1)
detail: OpenRouter extracts characters per scene when configured; rule-based fallback on no key or errors. PR #20; issue #9. HTTP calls mocked in tests.
issueBody:
As a director, I want the character breakdown drafted by the model, so that I review a model draft instead of a text parse.

Acceptance criteria:

- With `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set, `draft_breakdown` posts to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions`, and the page says "Drafted with the model."
- The request sends the scene text and takes the key from the environment. The key is not written into the prompt.
- With no key, or when the call fails, the page says "Drafted from the script text" and lists speakers found in the script.
- Tests cover model JSON, fenced JSON, a failed call, and the no-key path. They do not call OpenRouter.

Part of the script-breakdown story. Props, costumes, set pieces, and cues stay on that story.

title: Cast actors in roles (US-4)
detail: Link actors to script characters and their scenes. Issue #11.
issueBody:
As a director, I want to cast actors in roles, so that each actor sees their own scenes.

Acceptance criteria:

- A director can name a character and assign it to a member whose role is actor.
- An actor's page lists the scenes where that character speaks, and no others.
- Someone who is not a member cannot open the casting page.

title: Expand AI breakdown and review/save (US-3, part 2)
detail: Draft props, costumes, set pieces and lighting/sound cues; allow director to correct and save suggestions. Current implementation only drafts characters. Issue #9.
issueBody:
As a director, I want an AI draft of the script breakdown (characters per scene, props, costumes, set pieces, cues), so that I review it instead of building it by hand.

Acceptance criteria:

- Only a member can open the breakdown page.
- The server calls OpenRouter. Browser JavaScript does not.
- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` stays in the environment and never enters git.
- Tests mock the HTTP call and do not call OpenRouter.
- The draft lists characters per scene, props, costumes, set pieces, and cues.
- If the call fails, the page still shows a draft parsed from the script text.

The character list is the Sprint 2 slice. Props, costumes, set pieces, and cues are still open.

title: Schedule rehearsals (US-5)
detail: Select scenes, schedule sessions and determine which actors must attend; track scene readiness. Issue #12.
issueBody:
As a director, I want to schedule rehearsals for chosen scenes and see who must attend, so that I don't call people who aren't needed.

Acceptance criteria:

- A director can create a rehearsal with a start time and one or more scenes.
- The rehearsal lists the actors cast in those scenes.
- Actors who are not in those scenes are left off the call list.

title: Record rehearsal attendance (US-6)
detail: Stage manager records attendance and tracks missed rehearsals. Issue #13.
issueBody:
As a stage manager, I want to take attendance at a rehearsal, so that we track who missed what.

Acceptance criteria:

- A stage manager can mark each called actor present or absent.
- A director can view that record.
- An actor cannot change attendance.

title: Actor dashboard (US-7)
detail: Show assigned role, scenes, lines, rehearsal schedule and notes. Issue #14.
issueBody:
As an actor, I want to see my scenes, lines, rehearsal schedule and notes, so that I come prepared.

Acceptance criteria:

- An actor sees their character, the scenes they appear in, the text of those scenes, upcoming rehearsals, and notes from the director.
- They do not see another actor's notes.

title: Script-line cue sheet and printing (US-8)
detail: Persist line-level references and attach lighting, sound and set changes; print cue sheets. Issue #15.
issueBody:
As a stage manager, I want to attach lighting, sound and set cues to script lines and print a cue sheet, so that the crew can run the show.

Acceptance criteria:

- A stage manager can attach a lighting, sound, or set cue to a line.
- A cue sheet lists those cues in script order.
- An actor cannot edit cues.

title: Props, costumes, set & task tracker (US-9)
detail: Track production items and tasks with status and responsibility. Issue #16.
issueBody:
As a stage manager, I want to track props, costumes, set items and tasks, so that nothing is missing on opening night.

Acceptance criteria:

- A stage manager can add an item with a type (prop, costume, set, or task) and a status.
- The list can be filtered by type.
- An actor can view the list and cannot edit it.
